r0.why: Basic concept, transitions among three types through geologic time [1][5]; altered when forced out of equilibrium [2]; plate tectonics and water cycle as driving forces [4].

r1.why: Variably unstable in atmosphere [7], broken into fragments with dissolved material carried off [8], accumulation, burial, compaction [10], three lithification routes [12].

r2.why: High temperature and pressure make metamorphic rock [15], any pre-existing rock [20], regional over wide area with mountain building [16], contact with heating igneous intrusion [18][19].

r3.why: Deep rocks melt [21], cool and crystallize when not liquid [22], any type [26], slow intrusive cooling coarse like granite [23], lava cools rapidly [24], fine-grained or glass like obsidian [25].

r4.why: Plate tectonics recognized as driving force [35], new magma at mid-ocean divergent boundaries [36], rock carried from ridge as plates part [38], meets subduction zone [39], eclogite from rising P and T [40].

r5.why: Volatiles driven off into overlying wedge [41], wedge melts and buoyant magma gives island arc or continental margin volcanism [42]; basalt may break down and dissolve or melt on subduction [3].
